newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Harmony boosts Randgold Dec qtr profits.
newsitem.headline: Harmony boosts Randgold Dec qtr profits.

text.p: A strong performance by Harmony Gold Mining Co Ltd lifted Randgold and Exploration Co Ltd's December quarter after tax profits to 126.6 million rand from 74.98 million in the previous quarter.
"They were our best results ever," Randgold chairman Peter Flack told Reuters.

Harmony reported a 179 percent increase in after tax profit to 56.5 million from 20.2 million in the three months to end-September and the company said results for the March quarter were likely to be on par with the December results.
"It will be a benchmark quarter for Harmony in future," Harmony managing director Bernard Swanepoel said at the results presentation.

The mine lifted gold production seven percent to 5,282 kg from 4,911 kg in the previous quarter, while unit working costs were reduced to 45,017 rand/kg from 49,769 in the three months to end-December.
Tonnes milled increased to 1,333,000 tonnes from 1,270,000 in the previous quarter, while the average yield improved to 3.96 g/t from 3.87.
Harmony also received a much higher rand gold price of 56,151 rand against 55,098 rand in the previous quarter.

Swanepoel said in forecasting March quarter results that production and volume would remain constant, while costs would be contained. But the company expected to receive a rand gold price of around 54,000 rand/kg in the coming quarter.

Of Randgold's other mines, Blyvooruitzicht Gold Mining Co Ltd, increased its after-tax profit to 18.8 million rand from 11.4 million. The company said the increase could be attributed to an increase in underground gold production to 1,529 kg from 1,384 kg in the December quarter.
Buffelsfontein Gold Mines Ltd increased pre-tax profit to 31.3 million rand from 26.65 million in the previous quarter.

"In the process, it has repaid Gencor Ltd's 50 million rand loan, wiped out its accumulated losses and started paying mining tax again," the company said. Buffelsfontein's tax bill for the quarter was 7.40 million rand.
The Grootvlei Proprietary Mines Ltd reversed a 4.1 million after-tax loss in the September quarter and reported an after-tax profit of 2.02 million rand.
Increased underground production at East Rand Proprietary Mines Ltd lifted after-tax profits to 18.68 million rand from 15.02 million.

But ERPM managing director Ferdi Dippenaar said a decision was taken earlier in January to close the mine's L Shaft, which has been operating at a loss for some time. This meant the retrenchment of some 640 workers, he said.
